title: Microsoft 365 Copilot Without the Hype: Adoption, Governance & Getting Your Tenant Ready with Paul Keijzers [MVP]
description:
Buying Copilot licenses is easy, but Copilot then surfaces years of SharePoint, Teams and OneDrive content that was never meant to be shared. In this episode, Microsoft MVP Paul Keijzers explains to IT leaders and Microsoft 365 admins what a Copilot-ready tenant really means. You get practical advice on oversharing, Purview labels and DLP, content lifecycle, adoption and agent governance.
In this episode
00:00 – Is your tenant ready for Copilot?02:37 – Paul's journey from car audio to SharePoint and Copilot11:33 – What companies underestimate15:11 – Old SharePoint content and content lifecycle21:28 – Oversharing, Purview, labels and DLP30:17 – Adoption, champions and Copilot costs40:46 – Agents and Agent 36545:08 – Focus weeks and rapid fire round
Key takeaways
Copilot readiness is a Microsoft 365 project: start with sharing settings, permissions, retention, sensitivity labels and DLP, including Power Automate DLP for connectors.Old, unarchived SharePoint content and duplicate versions make Copilot look like it hallucinates, so archive or restrict content and keep metadata and folder structures simple.Strong adoption comes from continuous, outcome-focused support in the business rather than one-time training days, while token-based tools like Copilot Cowork need cost awareness.
Worth quoting
“they forget about permissions they forget about retention they forget about a DLP they forget about the labeling aspect” – Paul Keijzers (11:46)
“copilot readiness isn't really a copilot project it's Microsoft 365 project it's understand your share point environment it's understand who can access what” – Mirko Peters (53:21)
